findings.claim: secret/default/openfang/minio survived the purge, so r2 failed and the docs' "every key purged" was false.

verdict.text: The leftover openfang MinIO key is purged with all its versions, and a full recursive walk of the secret/ mount finds no path or field named minio.
The docs' claim that every old MinIO key was purged is now true.
The tree is unchanged since round 1 and the stamp is still green, so the ticket passes.

`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: `pass gate pre_commit`, `pass gate cli_tests`, `pass eval-row r1`, stamp green `f032c681eb3af42e51f330eb2ec6384cb7ed97fcb7a68e5bf820d50823bbcdf7`, the same tree as round 1.
Vault, live: `vault kv metadata get secret/default/openfang/minio` returns "No value found", so the metadata and every version are gone, not only soft-deleted.
`vault kv list secret/default/openfang` no longer lists `minio`.
I did not rely on the spike's two-level check, which only matches exact top-level names.
I walked the whole `secret/` mount recursively, with no depth limit: 123 paths, none matching `minio` (case-insensitive).
I also read every leaf's field names, without printing values, and none contains `minio`.

Spike 2 evidence (`.loop/spikes/minio-volume-destroy/2/`): no `minio_data` volume, host directory gone, and a plan holding only the 15 always-run `null_resource.firewall` replacements, the same as round 1.
Docs: `.okf/components/minio.md` lines 37-38 and 117-119 say every MinIO key under `default/minio/*` and `default/<job>/minio` was purged with all its versions.
The openfang key was purged with `vault kv metadata delete`.
My recursive walk of `secret/` finds no MinIO path left, so r2 holds and the purge claims in `.okf/components/minio.md` and `.okf/log.md` are true.
The openfang key was soft-deleted in April, when its job retired, so that wording is a little loose for that one key.
The purge claim that follows is correct, and this is not a finding.
